claim: The sprite engine has 1,824 clocks a line (1,792 at 48K timing): a sprite not on the line costs 1, one on it 1 + its drawn width in dots (17 unscaled, 129 at 8x), transparent dots included, and later sprites in the table are dropped.
limit: From the book, not measured here: it gives about 75 unscaled sprites when all sit on one line, where the Next wiki promises 100; plan for the lower figure and keep sprites that must show low in the table.

evidence.source: I. Novak, Unraveling the ZX Spectrum Next, Vol 1 (2026; core 3.03.03), chapter 16
evidence.text: The engine starts at sprite 0 each line; when it reaches a sprite inside that sprite's cut-off window near the end of the line it draws neither it nor any after it and sets bit 1 of port 0x303B, which stays set until read.
